problem_description: Compute the average temperature in K, pressure in bar, and density in kg/m^3 of a chloroform (CHCl3) liquid system solvated with water molecules.  The system consisted of 500 chloroform molecules and 2373 water molecules (SOL) in a cubic simulation box of dimensions 5.0 × 5.0 × 5.0 nm³ and was modeled using the gromos54a7_atb.ff force field. Energy minimization was carried out using the steepest descent algorithm for 10000 steps with an energy minimization step size of 0.002 nm using the Verlet cutoff scheme with neighbor list updates every step, and it should use the PME coulombic type and the rcoulomb and rvdw as 1.2 nm. Molecular dynamics simulations were performed using the md integrator with a time step of 0.001 ps for 10000 steps during the NPT equilibration stage with neighbor list updates every 5 steps. Non-bonded interactions were treated using a cut-off scheme with both electrostatic and van der Waals cutoffs of 1.4 nm. No bond constraints were applied during the simulations. Temperature coupling was applied using the Berendsen thermostat with a coupling constant of 0.1 ps and a reference temperature of 300 K. Pressure coupling was applied using the Berendsen barostat with a coupling constant of 5 ps and a reference pressure of 1.0 bar. The compressibility used for pressure coupling was 4.5e-5 bar⁻¹. Production simulations were then carried out using the md integrator with a time step of 0.001 ps for 100000 steps using the same thermostat and barostat parameters.
